name: platform-native-ladder
description: Harder platform-native use-case tasks for probing levels 6-8 of the capability ladder. Runtimes may use any native tools they expose; scoring is task-completion oriented.

tasks.prompt: Use your available tools to fetch live metadata for https://api.github.com/repos/ebelo/local-agent-bench. Answer with the repository full_name and default_branch. Do not use prior knowledge. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the command/tool, the URL, and the relevant output fields.

Use your available tools to fetch current weather for both Berlin, Germany and Zurich, Switzerland from a live web/API source. Answer with both cities and their current temperatures in Celsius, and say which is warmer. Do not invent values. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the command/tool, source URL(s), and relevant output.

Use your available tools to fetch the live README from https://raw.githubusercontent.com/ebelo/local-agent-bench/main/README.md and verify whether its capability ladder includes level 8 as end-to-end agent work. Answer yes or no, quote the relevant level 8 phrase, and cite the URL in an Evidence line.

Use your available tools to open benchmarks/native_nav/index.html, follow the links through the local HTML pages until you reach the final page, and tell me the navigation passphrase. Do not guess from filenames. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the files or links you followed and the relevant output.

Use your available tools to read benchmarks/native_nav/start.md, follow the Markdown links until the terminal note, and tell me the navigation code. Do not answer until you have followed the chain. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the files or links you followed and the relevant output.

Complete a small release-readiness brief. Use your available tools to read benchmarks/agentic/project.md, benchmarks/agentic/release.md, and benchmarks/agentic/grounding.md. Then fetch current weather for Zurich, Switzerland from a live source. Answer with a concise brief containing the project codename, release window, deployment color, current Zurich temperature in Celsius, and one go/no-go recommendation. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the files, command/tool, source URL, and relevant output.

Complete a small project-health task. Use your available tools to inspect pyproject.toml, run the local test suite with python3 -m pytest -q, and answer with the package name, whether there are runtime dependencies, the test result summary, and one concise health recommendation. In your final answer, include a short Evidence line naming the files/commands used and the relevant output.
